I've provided a command-line tool tauceti that should help you get started interacting with Tau Ceti.

uv tool install git+https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker.git

tauceti                            # the dashboard: see the available work, launch it
tauceti status                     # the same survey, non-interactive (--json for scripts)
tauceti work --only review         # one round of a specific kind of work, then exit
tauceti work --loop --only review  # a focused worker: keep reviewing (or fix / roadmap / ...)
tauceti work --loop                # fully automatic: keep picking the most useful job

• I hope that contributors will build their own tools: this is my idiosyncratic take on interacting with Tau Ceti, and many other approaches are possible!
  • tauceti by default uses the bubble sandboxing tool, discussed earlier on zulip. You can use the --host option to instead run unsandboxed (e.g., if you are already in a sandbox you trust more, or on a disposable machine)
  • tauceti assumes that you have gh auth set up, and interacts with the Tau Ceti repositories using that account.
I would be really excited to have someone else run tauceti work --loop --only review, and report back whether it is working!

(If you have a Codex or Claude subscription account, and are willing to use some tokens, this is an extremely easy way to help out. tauceti ensures that usage% < elapsed% for both the session and weekly windows in Codex or Claude subscriptions.)
It's also possible to use arbitrary review agents via openrouter and the pi harness. Please discuss here before pointing such agents at live PRs on Tau Ceti, however.

I spent a bit of time trying to get tauceti to work on my macOS laptop and there are a few blockers with my setup (the first two bullet points also apply similarly to bubble):

  • I have both personal and work Claude code subscriptions, which I switch between using CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. However, tauceti always reads from $HOME/.claude. (I guess it's possible to work around this, by setting up a symlink at random_directory/.claude.)
  • More importantly, on macOS, Claude Code stores the credentials in the Keychain, not in a .credentials.json file, and the worker doesn't support this, so Claude is always treated as unavailable.
  • It'd be nice if we could override the claude invocation with a TAUCETI_CLAUDE_CMD env var, to match PI_RUN, TAUCETI_BUBBLE, TAUCETI_CODEX_MODEL. That way I could route my own sandboxed claude into the worker.

I'll try and work around these locally in a clone of tauceti later; if you're interested I can also turn my changes into PR(s).
@Bryan Gin-ge Chen, the third point is now solved by https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker/pull/36.

And https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker/pull/37 should fix the first point. (Although I need to make a separate fix in bubble to support this, so for now the fix will only work with --host, i.e. disabling the bubble sandbox.)

I didn't end up following-up on this so I don't know if there's actually a problem there. If it turns out to be OK, then convenience functions would be appreciated!

Okay, the worker has been updated, and should work much better now.

uv tool install git+https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker.git
tauceti work --loop

is the minimum you need. This will try to use a local Codex or Claude subscription. See the README if you want something else.

If you run into errors about bubble and/or Incus, please tell me about them, and just add --host, but know you are then responsible for your own sandboxing!

If you want to work on a particular roadmap add e.g. --roadmap-focus HeegaardFloer or one of the other existing roadmaps. Or contribute a new roadmap! (Please someone try this! :-)

If you want your worker to only perform one action, use e.g. --only review, --only fix, or --only fix,fix-ci,roadmap, etc.

I tried running the worker with --only roadmap a few days ago and Claude ended up quitting without committing or pushing anything so I asked Claude to look into what happened today.

There seem to be two different issues:

  • I don't have push access to TauCeti so claim.sh acquire returned a 403. The worker continued on, even though the work it was creating could not be landed (without me creating a clone and pointing the worker there somehow).
  • Claude ended its turn with the work uncommitted (after getting the work building, it started a final background verify build, then stopped expecting to be resumed, which didn't happen of course since it was not in an interactive session). This is separate from kim-em/TauCetiWorker#64: that sweeps orphaned build-waiters in --loop, but (a) it doesn't make the work get committed/pushed, and (b) it doesn't run for a one-shot tauceti work, which is in-process. The agent should be told to verify synchronously and push before yielding.

The review agents, when using Codex, now try using Sol, and fall back to Terra is that is not available.

(You can force ./tauceti to only use Terra with export TAUCETI_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5.6-terra.)

I've also added an option --pace that lets you specify how much of subscription quotas are available for workers to use. You specify a pace by giving the hinge points of a piecewise linear function from "time elapsed %" to "max quota used %". The default behaviour is --pace 0:0,100:100, which says "quota used % < time elapsed %". You could instead say --pace 0:0,90:0,100:95, which says "you may not use any quota during the first 90% of the window, and then you may use up to 95% of the quota by the end of the window".
(Note that for Claude agents, the --pace argument applies both to the weekly and session quotas.0

Update: the default behaviour of ./tauceti is now to run "natively", i.e. without a bubble sandbox. (i.e. the default behaviour is what used to be tauceti --host.) To get the old behaviour use tauceti --bubble.

I've been testing tauceti for the last few days on my Mac, and I've posted some issues and a PR on GitHub based on my experience. Let me know if this is the right venue, or if you'd rather just have the feedback here.

Some additional thoughts:

Running in bubble mode presented some challenges. By default it downloads mathlib and builds Tau Ceti from scratch each time, so each round would take almost 1.5 hours. I could get the mathlib cache to work, but the Tau Ceti build still took ~40 minutes of hogging ~all of my CPU. I felt like this was a big unnecessary drain on my resources, so I abandoned it. But maybe it could work with a better system for caching Tau Ceti builds.

I also tried running in host mode for a few rounds. This was a much better experience performance wise, but it's not a sustainable option for security reasons.

A third option is to run the entire ./tauceti process in a container. This has the host benefit of persistent memory between rounds with the security benefit of running in a sandbox environment. If interested in trying this, I made a docker container, but keep in mind that this is still very experimental.

I've now adopted @Eivind Otto Hjelle's docker setup. There's a section in the README on using it.

On first use:

docker compose build
docker compose run --rm auth gh auth login --git-protocol https
docker compose run --rm auth codex login --device-auth
docker compose run --rm auth claude auth login

(Only one of codex login and claude auth login is needed.)

Then, to start a worker which works on all available tasks:

docker compose up -d

To watch its progress:

docker compose logs -f tauceti claude-refresh codex-refresh

To shut down the worker:

docker compose down

If you want to pass arguments to the worker, e.g. to have it work only on particular phases (review, fix-ci, fix, roadmap) or only work on particular roadmaps, you can use e.g.:

TAUCETI_WORKER_ARGS="--only fix,fix-ci,roadmap --roadmap-only CombinatorialHeegaardFloer" docker-compose up -d
